task: E11: does a STRONGER non-linear readout overturn D1? (zero GPU)
threads_why: Same requirement as E16: the probe is not bit-reproducible across BLAS thread counts. The linear arm imports e8_analyse.probe verbatim, so 4 threads is the only setting in which its output can be compared to E8's delivered numbers.

readouts.nystrom: RBF Nystrom map (512 comps, gamma from the training fold) + L2 logistic
readouts.mlp: 2-layer, 256 hidden, FULL input (no PCA), max_iter 5000, convergence checked

gate_why: A readout more than 0.01 AUC below the linear baseline is barred from the verdict (E11_PREREG.md Q2). Without this gate the MLP would appear to 'prove' capacity matters (D1 77-87%) when it is actually over-fitting on n~750 (all folds converged, so this is generalisation failure, not an optimisation failure): AUC_random collapses to 0.50-0.60 while AUC_real barely moves, which shrinks D1's denominator and raises D1 mechanically.

selfcheck.rule: the linear arm must reproduce E8's delivered D1 on every cell

vjepa_special_case.why: V-JEPA's LikePhys D1 is not a single-seed quantity: E15/E16 measured 43.8-54.0% across probe partitions. Its cells are read from the six-partition means, so the linear baseline reproduces the delivered 49.4%.
vjepa_special_case.single_seed_would_have_been: linear 51.11% at seed 1000 (E11_cells.json), which would NOT have reproduced E8's delivered 49.4%; the six-partition mean is what makes the comparison valid

scope_limits: only 4 cells, chosen because capacity can only flip a verdict near the 50% bar
only ONE non-linear family (Nystrom) survives the gate; the strongest readout class (temporal attention probe, Punzo et al. 2606.09646) is NOT tested
no cross-model comparison is drawn from these numbers
